the_trade_off_made: We favored damage (user impact and work blockage) over pure deadline urgency and revenue considerations. This may delay revenue‑generating enterprise customers and risk their satisfaction, but it prevents larger operational disruption.
hardest_call: Placing the feature request (TICK-00266) after the overdue export failure (TICK-00982) was the closest call; the export is overdue but the feature request has a deadline in 0.3 h, so it could reasonably have been ranked third.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.why: Damage captures the real harm to users and business operations, which aligns with our policy and the most critical tickets.

rejected.money: Prioritising money would have pushed high‑paying enterprise tickets ahead of critical incidents, leaving severe outages for later.
rejected.damage: N/A – this was the chosen metric.
rejected.deadline: A deadline‑first approach would have moved the near‑deadline feature request ahead of the overdue export, potentially increasing user frustration.
rejected.fairness: Fairness would have treated tickets more equally but would not have highlighted the extreme impact of the security breach and data loss.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.what_it_costs_us: Focusing on damage may delay addressing high‑value paying customers, risking churn or dissatisfaction.

reasons_the_data_did_not_support.the_model_said: A feature request with a deadline in minutes is urgent but less damaging than the overdue export issue.

reasons_we_asked_the_model_to_rewrite.TICK-00266: The ticket sits relatively high because its response window is almost exhausted (only 0.3 hours left) and it comes from an Enterprise‑paying customer, giving it strong money and deadline signals. While monitoring shows low severity, a single user impact and no work blockage, the urgency of the deadline and the revenue from the customer outweigh the low damage rating, placing it ahead of tickets with looser deadlines or lower‑paying accounts.

reasons_before_correction.TICK-00771: Potential account takeover is a security risk and policy forces it into the top three.
reasons_before_correction.TICK-00171: Massive data loss affecting thousands and blocking work demands immediate attention despite the customer paying nothing.
reasons_before_correction.TICK-00982: The export failure is already overdue and blocks many users, making it the highest damage among remaining tickets.

reasons_before_correction.TICK-00707: Slow performance affects only a few users and is low severity, so it follows higher‑impact tickets.
reasons_before_correction.TICK-00135: Password reset is low impact and has ample time before the SLA deadline, placing it last.
